   3 years ago


I am really struggling with this glaze. The test tiles came out
beautifully. When I made the large batch, however, I got a sky
blue consistently. It did run quite a bit which I chalked up to
students applying to much glaze. (Many beginners). The second
try, I thinned it a bit, which then made the application to thin. The
glaze fell out of suspension within minutes. I added Epsom salts
solution which helped some. Then the application of the glaze
was problematic. It would crack and fall of the pot. This last time
the glaze went on better, I told them no more than one layer of
glaze. Most pots kept their glaze. One pot had flaking where it

overlapped, from glazing one side then the other. Out of the kiln
though, the color was thin and all washed out, like the yellow
green stain referenced above. I really hate to give up on this
glaze but I am at a loss. It's very frustrating for both myself and
the students. Any help would be appreciated.

   Anne W
    10 months ago


I am early in my glaze-making journey, and this is the first one I
made that I absolutely love. Seems to come out a little lighter
and more towards turquoise on brown stoneware and more like
the deep blue in the thumbnail on white stoneware, though it
sounds like the level of reduction also plays a role in that. My
batch did turn out to be slightly runny, so will mostly use on the
insides and rims of things. Poured/dipped application worked
well, less happy with brushing it on.
